messages.body_plain:
No problem - also to add to what David said, note the micro_era5 function in NicheMapR (the paper describing it is currently in review). Check the help for it to see how you can directly run the microclimate model with the ERA-5 reanalysis as the forcing data with the help of the mcera package. But be warned - at the moment the latter takes a while to download the data so it's best to get it and store it locally.

All the best,
Mike

> > Hi Esther
> >
> > You can try using meteorological reanalysis data for the variables that you are missing.  The European Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasting has produced the ERA-5 reanalysis at a 0.25 degree lat lon grid and 1 hour resolution worldwide.  You can get data from https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/cdsapp#!/search?type=dataset&text=era5 .  You have to register with them to do downloads but the data are free.  An alternative source is the NCAR/UCAR Research Data Archive in the USA : https://rda.ucar.edu/datasets/ds633.0/.   ERA-5 data are available hourly from 1950 onward.  You can get regional subsets of the data from rda.ucar.edu <http://rda.ucar.edu> or the Copernicus Data Store.
> >
> > An alternative dataset is NASA  Modern-Era Retrospective analysis for Research and Applications, Version 2 (MERRA-2).  See https://gmao.gsfc.nasa.gov/reanalysis/MERRA-2/docs/  for more information. It is hourly from the 1980s, on a  0.625 x 0.5 degree grid.  Regional subsetting is available.

NOAA has similar products from their two geostationary satellites over the Americas https://www.goes-r.gov/products/baseline-DSR.html . In all of these cases you need to register with the websites, but you don't have to pay for the data. messages.subject_clean: Possible to estimate water temperature from a microclimate model?
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,
I am new to NicheMapR and I would like clarification on two questions.
1. Is it possible to estimate water temperature from a hypothetical pool of water  (e.g. pond or small lake) using NicheMapR? I attempted the following code with the guidelines from the tutorial:
data.frame(NicheMapR::micro_global(loc = c(128.0538, 36.812702), # Korea as the location
                                                 runshade = 0,
                                                 minshade = 0,
                                                 maxshade = 10, # Will be testing the effects of low shade and high shade on water temperatures later on.
                                                 PCTWET   = 100, # Model surface soil wetness assuming 100 % wetness (simulates water?)
                                                 maxpool  = 400 # Max depth for water pooling on the surface (hypothetical pond 400 mm deep).
)$soil) # I assume soil would be the appropriate choice.

If this is not correct, could someone point me in the right direction with the correct model input?

2. If estimating water temperature from microclimate models is possible, is there a way to predict the effects of climate warming on the model? Such as a future RCP8.5 projection at 2050. What inputs would I need to change?

Regards,
Nicholas

https://github.com/everydayduffy/mcera5

messages.subject: Running NicheMapR & running NicheMapR inside
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone!

I was hoping I might ask some advice on which is the path of least resistance.

I've got seasonal data of a burrowing ectotherm sp. change in mass after being kept outside and inside (at a fairly consistent temperature) for periods of several weeks, plus the mass of their brood balls.

As some of the features of the microclimate model (including necessary argument longlat) can't be included for accurate results for the inside treatment, am I better off manually overriding specific variables, or making data tables to replicate micro global?

Many thanks,

messages.subject_clean: Possible to estimate water temperature from a microclimate model?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Nick,

Check out a previous post on this form March this year under the title "simulating pond temperatures". There are two ways to roughly simulate a pool of water with NicheMapR. One is as you suggested, where you set the soil to be high in clay, and you can also set a multiplier on the rainfall to simulate a catchment (rainmult parameter). I've found this to work very well in simulating wetland dynamics in terms of water depth. There is no calculation of temperature here though. You could get a rough idea of this by simulating water-logged soil of low bulk density and seeing what that gives you at different depths. The other approach is to use the container model of the ectotherm model which will give you a water temperature (for the 'core' of the pool).

Re simulating climate change effects, to do this you need to feed the microclimate model the future climate change scenario conditions.

All the best,
Mike

messages.body_plain:
Hi Zhong-wen (and Dave),

I tried it too and had the same problem. The main thing is that it starts off under very cold conditions with a large rainfall event, which is hard for the integrator in terms of the snow calculation (it works fine with the snow model turned off). So you can either start it in summer (best solution), or increase the ERR parameter (I got it to complete with ERR = 5).

Note also that your code for specifying the dates puts a space before the year:

dstart=paste("01/03/",1985,spe="")
dfinish=paste("31/10/",1985,sep="")

which does cause a problem when the R code uses those dates to get the number of years (I need an error trap for this input). Instead use:

dstart=paste0("01/03/",1985)
dfinish=paste0("31/10/",1985).

All the best,
Mike
